neighbours.label: In code, an identifier part naming one member of a paired/ordered family (min/max, start/end, old/new, lower/upper, major/minor, x/y/z), inside names built on a sibling pattern seen on nearby lines

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, random arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Top examples are code identifier fragments (min, start, old, .major, lower, x) that are one member of a sibling pair/triple, and the - pole fires on the z/w end of x,y,z; band samples show weak spread across numbers and variable parts in code and some prose, so coverage is likely poor. Label is a guess at a distinction (sibling-pair names) rather than a single token.
